hero.caption: The site of Bledsoe's Station in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  Bledsoe's Station was a frontier fort built in the early 1780s to protect settlers from Native American attacks.  Archaeological excavations in the late 1990s verified the fort's location.  The fort is no longer standing, but excavation trench lines give visitors an idea of the fort's layout.

images.caption: The Cheskiki Mound site in Castalian Springs, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  The site was once home to a substantial Mississippian-period (c. 1000-1400 A.D.) Native American village.  The burial mound at the center is one of 12 known mounds at the site.

images.caption: Sign marking a section of Avery's Trace at Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  Avery's Trace was an 18th-century wagon road connecting East and Middle Tennessee.

images.caption: Hugh Rogan Cottage (also known as "Rogana") at Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  Hugh Rogan (1747-1814), a Tennessee frontiersman, built the cottage sometime around 1800.  The cottage's design reflects folk traditions of Rogan's native Ireland.  The cottage was dismantled and moved to Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in 1998.

images.caption: The Nathaniel Parker Cabin at Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  The cabin was built by Tennessee frontiersman Nathaniel Parker in the 1780s.  The cabin was originally located near Greenfield a few miles to the north.

images.caption: The entrance to the Cavern of the Skulls at Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  Cave explorers in the 1800s reported human skulls in the cave, suggesting that the cave may have been used to store "trophy" skulls captured by the inhabitants of the Cheskiki Mound village to the east.  The cave is gated off and not open to the public.

images.caption: Belote Cemetery, also called the "Pioneer Cemetery," at Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  The cemetery contains the graves of the family of Jeremiah Belote, who settled in the area in 1807, and several other early settlers.  A monument to frontiersmen Anthony and Isaac Bledsoe is located in the back of the cemetery.

images.caption: Monument dedicated to Anthony Bledsoe (1733-1788) and Isaac Bledsoe (c. 1735-1793) at Bledsoe's Fort Historical Park in Sumner County, Tennessee, in the southeastern United States.  The monument, located at the back of Belote Cemetery, was erected by the Bledsoes' descendants in 1908.
